content.text:
# Finding Pairs (a, b) with ab + a + b = 2026 and gcd(a, b) = 1

## Setting Up the Factorization

I use the standard technique of adding 1 to both sides:

$$ab + a + b + 1 = 2027$$

$$(a+1)(b+1) = 2027$$

## Factoring 2027

I check divisibility by all primes up to $\lfloor\sqrt{2027}\rfloor = 45$:

| Prime p | 2027 ÷ p | Divisible? |
|---------|----------|------------|
| 2 | 1013.5 | No |
| 3 | 675.7… | No (digit sum = 11) |
| 5 | 405.4 | No |
| 7 | 289.6… | No |
| 11 | 184.3… | No |
| 13 | 155.9… | No |
| 17 | 119.2… | No |
| 19 | 106.7… | No |
| 23 | 88.1… | No |
| 29 | 69.9… | No |
| 31 | 65.4… | No |
| 37 | 54.8… | No |
| 41 | 49.4… | No |
| 43 | 47.1… | No |

**2027 is prime.**

## Conclusion

Since 2027 is prime, the only factorization into positive integers is $1 \times 2027$, which gives $(a, b) = (0, 2026)$ — but $a = 0$ is **not** a positive integer.

$$\boxed{\text{There are no such pairs.}}$$
